If the user already controls binding via OMP_PROC_BIND / OMP_PLACES /\n// GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY, leave it to the runtime.\nvoid pinThreads() {\n    if (getenv(\"OMP_PROC_BIND\") || getenv(\"OMP_PLACES\") || getenv(\"GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY\")) return;\n    cpu_set_t allowed;\n    CPU_ZERO(&allowed);\n    if (sched_getaffinity(0, sizeof(allowed), &allowed) != 0) return;\n    std::vector<int> cpus;\n    for (int c = 0; c < CPU_SETSIZE; ++c) {\n        if (CPU_ISSET(c, &allowed)) cpus.push_back(c);\n    }\n    if (cpus.empty()) return;\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        const int t = omp_get_thread_num();\n        cpu_set_t one;\n        CPU_ZERO(&one);\n        CPU_SET(cpus[(size_t)t % cpus.size()], &one);\n        sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(one), &one);\n    }\n}\n\n// Allocate a grid without serial zero-fill: reserve, request transparent huge\n// pages, and let the parallel first-touch (in the same z/y distribution the\n// stencil uses) place pages on the NUMA node of the thread that will use them.\nvoid allocateGrid(std::vector<Real>& grid, const size_t n) {\n    grid.reserve(n);\n    const size_t bytes = n * sizeof(Real);\n    const uintptr_t beg = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(grid.data());\n    const uintptr_t pg = (uintptr_t)sysconf(_SC_PAGESIZE);\n    const uintptr_t abeg = (beg + pg - 1) & ~(pg - 1);\n    const uintptr_t aend = (beg + bytes) & ~(pg - 1);\n    if (aend > abeg) {\n        madvise(reinterpret_cast<void*>(abeg), aend - abeg, MADV_HUGEPAGE);  // best-effort hint\n    }\n}\n\n// Resize after the storage has been first-touched; for a trivial element type\n// this is a (serial, untimed) zero-fill that does not change page placement.\nvoid commitGrid(std::vector<Real>& grid, const size_t n) {\n    grid.resize(n);\n}\n\nvoid initializeGrid'''\ns=s.replace('\\nvoid initializeGrid',helpers,1)\n\ns=s.replace('''// Touch (zero) a buffer in parallel with the same distribution as the stencil\n// so that both grids have matching NUMA page placement.\nvoid firstTouchGrid(std::vector<Real>& grid, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {\n    Real* __restrict g = grid.data();''','''// Touch (zero) a buffer in parallel with the same distribution as the stencil\n// so that both grids have matching NUMA page placement. Operates on reserved\n// storage, so `g` is passed explicitly.\nvoid firstTouchGrid(Real* __restrict g, const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz) {''')\n\ns=s.replace('''    // Allocate grids (double buffering)\n    std::vector<Real> grid1(gridSize);\n    std::vector<Real> grid2(gridSize);\n    \n    // Initialize\n    printf(\"Initializing grid...\\\\n\");\n    initializeGrid(grid1, nx, ny, nz);\n    firstTouchGrid(grid2, nx, ny, nz);\n''','''    pinThreads();\n\n    // Allocate grids (double buffering)\n    std::vector<Real> grid1;\n    std::vector<Real> grid2;\n    allocateGrid(grid1, gridSize);\n    allocateGrid(grid2, gridSize);\n    \n    // Initialize (parallel first touch), then commit the vector sizes\n    printf(\"Initializing grid...\\\\n\");\n    firstTouchGrid(grid1.data(), nx, ny, nz);\n    firstTouchGrid(grid2.data(), nx, ny, nz);\n    commitGrid(grid1, gridSize);\n    commitGrid(grid2, gridSize);\n    initializeGrid(grid1, nx, ny, nz);\n''')\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\nmake -C /tmp/omp 2>&1 | grep -E \"warning|error|Built\"; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011CgaaWAjWXPQPzvQ1E7yGf","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01Wn4v386HornZ4z74w9xE3U","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"python3 - <<'EOF'\np='stencil3d.cpp'; s=open(p).read()\nold=s[s.index('// Pin each OpenMP thread'):s.index('// Allocate a grid without')]\nnew='''// Read a small integer-list sysfs file such as \"0-3,128-131\"; returns false on failure.\nstatic bool readCpuList(const char* path, std::vector<int>& out) {\n    FILE* f = fopen(path, \"r\");\n    if (!f) return false;\n    char buf[4096];\n    size_t len = fread(buf, 1, sizeof(buf) - 1, f);\n    fclose(f);\n    buf[len] = '\\\\0';\n    char* p = buf;\n    while (*p) {\n        char* end;\n        long a = strtol(p, &end, 10);\n        if (end == p) break;\n        long b = a;\n        p = end;\n        if (*p == '-') {\n            b = strtol(p + 1, &end, 10);\n            p = end;\n        }\n        for (long c = a; c <= b; ++c) out.push_back((int)c);\n        while (*p == ',' || *p == ' ' || *p == '\\\\n') ++p;\n    }\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Build a CPU ordering for pinning: physical cores first (one CPU per core),\n// interleaved across NUMA nodes, followed by SMT siblings. With this order the\n// first T threads use T distinct cores spread evenly over all memory\n// controllers, which maximizes aggregate bandwidth for any thread count.\nstatic std::vector<int> buildCpuOrder(const std::vector<int>& allowed) {\n    std::vector<int> nodeOf(CPU_SETSIZE, 0);\n    std::vector<char> primary(CPU_SETSIZE, 1);\n    int maxNode = 0;\n    char path[256];\n    for (int node = 0; node < 1024; ++node) {\n        snprintf(path, sizeof(path), \"/sys/devices/system/node/node%d/cpulist\", node);\n        std::vector<int> cpus;\n        if (!readCpuList(path, cpus)) {\n            if (node > 0) break;\n            continue;\n        }\n        for (int c : cpus) if (c >= 0 && c < CPU_SETSIZE) nodeOf[c] = node;\n        maxNode = node;\n    }\n    for (int c : allowed) {\n        snprintf(path, sizeof(path), \"/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu%d/topology/thread_siblings_list\", c);\n        std::vector<int> sib;\n        if (readCpuList(path, sib) && !sib.empty()) {\n            // The lowest-numbered *allowed* sibling is the primary for its core\n            int lowest = -1;\n            for (int sc : sib) {\n                if (std::binary_search(allowed.begin(), allowed.end(), sc) && (lowest < 0 || sc < lowest)) lowest = sc;\n            }\n            primary[c] = (lowest == c) ? 1 : 0;\n        }\n    }\n    std::vector<int> order;\n    order.reserve(allowed.size());\n    for (int pass = 1; pass >= 0; --pass) {  // primaries first, then siblings\n        std::vector<std::vector<int>> perNode(maxNode + 1);\n        for (int c : allowed) {\n            if (primary[c] == pass) perNode[nodeOf[c]].push_back(c);\n        }\n        bool more = true;\n        for (size_t i = 0; more; ++i) {\n            more = false;\n            for (auto& v : perNode) {\n                if (i < v.size()) { order.push_back(v[i]); more = true; }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    return order;\n}\n\n// Pin each OpenMP thread to a distinct CPU from the process's allowed CPU set.\n// Unpinned threads migrate between cores/NUMA nodes, which destroys cache\n// locality and first-touch NUMA placement for a bandwidth-bound stencil. If\n// the user already controls binding via OMP_PROC_BIND / OMP_PLACES /\n// GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY, leave it to the runtime.\nvoid pinThreads() {\n    if (getenv(\"OMP_PROC_BIND\") || getenv(\"OMP_PLACES\") || getenv(\"GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY\")) return;\n    cpu_set_t allowedSet;\n    CPU_ZERO(&allowedSet);\n    if (sched_getaffinity(0, sizeof(allowedSet), &allowedSet) != 0) return;\n    std::vector<int> allowed;\n    for (int c = 0; c < CPU_SETSIZE; ++c) {\n        if (CPU_ISSET(c, &allowedSet)) allowed.push_back(c);\n    }\n    if (allowed.empty()) return;\n    const std::vector<int> order = buildCpuOrder(allowed);\n    if (order.empty()) return;\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        const int t = omp_get_thread_num();\n        cpu_set_t one;\n        CPU_ZERO(&one);\n        CPU_SET(order[(size_t)t % order.size()], &one);\n        sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(one), &one);\n    }\n}\n\n'''\ns=s.replace(old,new)\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF\nmake -C /tmp/omp 2>&1 | grep -E \"warning|error|Built\"; for n in 64 33 5; do /tmp/base/stencil3d -x $n -y $((n+3)) -z $((n-1)) -i 7 -r -v | grep -vE \"time|Perf|threads\" > /tmp/b.txt; /tmp/omp/stencil3d -x $n -y $((n+3)) -z $((n-1)) -i 7 -r -v | grep -vE \"time|Perf|threads\" > /tmp/o.txt; diff /tmp/b.txt /tmp/o.txt && echo \"n=$n IDENTICAL\"; done\nfor t in 1 2 4 8 16 32 64 128 256; do echo -n \"T=$t: \"; OMP_NUM_THREADS=$t /tmp/omp/stencil3d -x 512 -i 10 | grep -E \"Perf\"; done; echo -n \"default 256^3: \"; /tmp/omp/stencil3d -x 256 -i 10 | grep Perf; echo -n \"default 128^3: \"; /tmp/omp/stencil3d | grep Perf; echo -n \"base 128^3: \"; /tmp/base/stencil3d | grep Perf","description":"Add topology-aware CPU ordering for pinning, rebuild, verify and benchmark scaling"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4192,"cache_read_input_tokens":25538,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4192},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"9f7a69fa-d19a-4265-8778-ca8c4e7c2963","uuid":"12ee358d-4c3c-4c81-b633-942b3a6e28a7","timestamp":"2026-10-31T15:49:25.467Z","request_id":"req_011CgaaWAKDQQ8Ak5HGr4aZf"}

Only the two existing files changed, the executable is still `stencil3d`, and output is bit-identical to the original.\n\n**What changed in `stencil3d/stencil3d.cpp`**\n\n- **Stencil kernel.** The interior loop and the boundary-copy loop are fused into one pass over (z, y) rows, distributed with a collapsed static `omp for`. Boundary rows are copied whole; interior rows compute the 7-point average with a SIMD inner loop and copy the two x-edge cells. The arithmetic expression and evaluation order are unchanged, so results match exactly.\n- **One parallel region for all iterations.** The iteration loop runs inside a single `omp parallel` region. Each iteration ends with a barrier, so there is no per-iteration fork and join cost.\n- **NUMA-aware allocation.** The grids are reserved, hinted for transparent huge pages, and first-touched in parallel with the same row distribution the stencil uses. The original value-initialization would have faulted every page on the main thread.\n- **Thread pinning.** Threads are pinned to distinct CPUs read from sysfs topology. Physical cores are chosen first and spread over NUMA nodes, then grouped by node so adjacent thread IDs share a node. If OMP_PROC_BIND, OMP_PLACES or GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY is set, the runtime's binding is respected instead.\n- **Validation** uses parallel reductions for the NaN check and min/max.\n- The program prints the OpenMP thread count at startup.\n\n**`stencil3d/CMakeLists.txt`** adds `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. No new external dependencies.\n\n**Correctness.** Sum, min, max, hash and sampled values from the results printer are identical to the original binary for cubic, non-cubic and degenerate grids (sizes 1, 2, 5, 33, 64, 512, zero and one iteration).\n\n**Performance** on this 2-socket, 128-core EPYC (measured memory bandwidth is only about 100 GB/s, so the kernel is bandwidth-bound):\n\n| Case | Original | OpenMP |\n|---|---|---|\n| 512³, 10 iterations, all 256 threads | 393 MCU/s | 8,727 MCU/s |\n| 128³, 200 iterations, default threads | 400 MCU/s | 17,395 MCU/s |\n| 512³, 1 thread | 393 MCU/s | 663 MCU/s |\n\nOne finding worth knowing: with threads spread round-robin across the two NUMA nodes, neighbouring z-planes live on opposite sockets and throughput fell to about a tenth. Grouping thread IDs by node is what makes the high thread counts scale.\n\nBuild and run as before:\n\n```\ncmake -S stencil3d -B build && cmake --build build\n./build/stencil3d -x 512 -i 10 -v\n```"}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":32,"cache_creation_input_tokens":770,"cache_read_input_tokens":39459,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":770},"output_tokens":767,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"9f7a69fa-d19a-4265-8778-ca8c4e7c2963","uuid":"51c3eef0-eb19-408a-8b29-a008003f9b3a","timestamp":"2026-10-31T15:51:37.467Z","request_id":"req_011CgaahTvBHme1MdYguxn3W"}
